lessons.title: Input, output and variables
lessons.summary: Read data in, store it, print it back out.
lessons.notes:
A program runs one line at a time, top to bottom. That order is called **sequence**.

- `input()` reads one line of text typed by the user.
- A **variable** stores a value so you can use it later: `name = input()`.
- `print()` sends a value to the screen.
- Everything `input()` gives you is a **string**. Use `int()` or `float()` to turn it into a number before doing maths.

In OCR exam wording, look for the words *read*, *accept*, *ask the user* (they mean `input()`) and *display*, *output*, *report* (they mean `print()`).
lessons.worked_example:
# Ask for a name and an age, then report back
name = input()
age = int(input())
next_year = age + 1
print(f"{name} will be {next_year} next year")
lessons.worked_example_note: `int(input())` reads a line and converts it to a whole number in one step. The f-string drops the variables straight into the message.

lessons.title: Arithmetic and rounding
lessons.summary: Calculations, integer division and formatting numbers.
lessons.notes:
Python arithmetic operators you need for OCR:

| Operator | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `+ - * /` | add, subtract, multiply, divide | `7 / 2` is `3.5` |
| `//` | integer (whole) division | `7 // 2` is `3` |
| `%` | remainder (modulus) | `7 % 2` is `1` |
| `**` | to the power of | `3 ** 2` is `9` |

`round(value, 2)` rounds to 2 decimal places. Watch the difference between `/` (always gives a decimal) and `//` (drops the decimal part completely).
lessons.worked_example:
# Convert a number of minutes into hours and minutes
total = int(input())
hours = total // 60
mins = total % 60
print(f"{hours} hours {mins} minutes")
lessons.worked_example_note: `//` and `%` work as a pair: one gives how many whole lots fit, the other gives what is left over.

lessons.title: Exam-style sequencing problems
lessons.summary: Longer scenarios where you decide the steps yourself.
lessons.notes:
Exam questions rarely say "use a variable". They describe a situation and leave you to work out the steps.

A reliable method:
1. Underline every value the program must **read in**.
2. Underline every value it must **output**, and the exact wording.
3. Write the calculation that gets from one to the other.

If the question gives an example of the output, copy the format exactly — spaces, capital letters and units all count. Where a question shows a specific example value, remember your program has to work for *any* valid input, not just that one example.
lessons.worked_example:
# A shop adds 20% VAT to every price.
# Read a price and display the price including VAT to 2 decimal places.
price = float(input())
with_vat = price * 1.2
print(round(with_vat, 2))
lessons.worked_example_note: Adding 20% is the same as multiplying by 1.2. Rounding happens last, after the maths.

quiz.question: What does input() always return?
options: An integer if the user types a number
quiz.explanation: input() always returns text, even if the user types digits — you must cast it explicitly to use it as a number.

quiz.question: Which exam words usually mean input()?
What does the line name = input() do, exactly?
options: Pauses for the user to type something, then stores it under name
quiz.answer: Pauses for the user to type something, then stores it under name

quiz.question: What does 7 // 2 evaluate to?
quiz.explanation: // is integer division — it drops the decimal part rather than rounding.

quiz.question: What does 7 % 2 evaluate to?
quiz.explanation: % gives the remainder after dividing — 7 divided by 2 is 3 remainder 1.

quiz.question: An exam question shows one example of correct output. What does that tell you?
options: The exact format your output must match — spacing, capitals and units all count
That your program only needs to work for that one example
That you can ignore the format shown
quiz.answer: The exact format your output must match — spacing, capitals and units all count

quiz.question: Before writing any code for a scenario question, what's the first step?
options: Work out exactly what must be read in and what must be output
quiz.answer: Work out exactly what must be read in and what must be output

quiz.question: A question shows one example input/output pair. Should your program only work for that exact example?
options: No — it must work for any valid input, the example is just a check
Yes, only that example needs to work
quiz.answer: No — it must work for any valid input, the example is just a check

tasks.title: Print a message
tasks.brief: Input one line of text. Print it back exactly as it was typed.
hints: Reading and printing are two separate steps — store what you read before printing it.
Store the result of input() under a name, then print that same name.

tasks.title: Double a number
tasks.brief:
Input a whole number. Print it multiplied by 2.

For example, if 5 is entered, print 10.
hints: Text can't be multiplied like a number — convert it with int() first.
Cast the input to a whole number, then multiply the stored value before printing it.

tasks.title: Add two numbers
tasks.brief: Input two whole numbers, one per line. Print their total.
hints: Call input() twice and store each value in its own variable before adding them.
Cast both inputs to whole numbers, store each separately, then add the two variables together.

tasks.title: Full name
tasks.brief:
Input a first name, then a surname — two separate lines. Print them on one line, separated by a single space.

For example, Ada then Lovelace prints as `Ada Lovelace`.
hints: An f-string keeps the spacing easy to see and get right.
An f-string like `f"{a} {b}"` places a literal space between two variables.

tasks.title: Name, reversed
tasks.brief:
Read a first name, then a surname — two separate lines, the same as before. This time print the surname first, then the first name, each on its own line (not on one line together).

For example, if the input is Ada then Lovelace, print Lovelace then Ada, each on its own line.
hints: You already have both values stored — this is about the order you print() them in, not about reading them differently.
Store both values first — then you're free to print() them in whichever order is asked for.

tasks.title: Seconds to minutes
tasks.brief:
A stopwatch records a time in seconds. Input the number of seconds. Display the whole minutes and the remaining seconds in the format `<minutes> min <seconds> s`.

For example, 150 seconds prints as `2 min 30 s`.
hints: // gives whole minutes (how many whole lots of 60 fit in). % gives the seconds left over.
Use // for the whole-minutes part and % for the remainder, then build the output with an f-string in the exact format shown.

tasks.title: Average of three marks
tasks.brief:
A teacher records three test marks. Input the three marks, one per line. Display the mean of all three, rounded to 1 decimal place.

For example, marks of 10, 11 and 12 give a mean of 11.0.
hints: Add the three marks together, then divide the total by 3.
Add all three values together, divide by how many there are, then round() the result to the stated decimal places.

tasks.title: Change from a note
tasks.brief:
A customer pays with a £10 note. Input the cost of the item as a decimal. Display the change, rounded to 2 decimal places.

For example, an item costing 3.5 gives change of 6.5.
hints: float(input()) reads a decimal value. Change is 10 minus the cost.
Cast to a float, work out the difference from the fixed amount given, then round the result before printing.

tasks.title: Perimeter and area
tasks.brief:
Input the width, then the height, of a rectangle — both whole numbers. Display the area on the first line. Display the perimeter on the second line.

For example, a width of 3 and height of 4 give an area of 12 and a perimeter of 14.
hints: Area is width times height. Perimeter is 2 * (width + height).
Cast both inputs, then print each calculated result on its own line, in the order asked for.

tasks.title: Tip, total and share
tasks.brief:
A group of friends is splitting a restaurant bill.

Read the bill amount as a decimal. Read the tip percentage as a whole number, for example 15 for 15%. Read the number of people splitting the bill as a whole number.

Calculate the tip amount: bill × tip percentage ÷ 100. Calculate the total: bill plus tip. Calculate each person's share: total ÷ number of people.

Print three lines, all rounded to 2 decimal places, in the format:
```
Tip: 6.0
Total: 46.0
Each pays: 11.5
```
hints: Work out tip, then total, then share, storing each in its own variable before you print anything.
Each value in the notes' formula depends on the one before it — round each as you go, not just at the very end.

tasks.title: Sponsored walk
tasks.brief:
A student is doing a sponsored walk for charity. Sponsors pay a fixed amount for every complete kilometre walked.

Read the distance walked in kilometres, a whole number. Read the amount paid per kilometre, a decimal. Report the total amount raised, rounded to 2 decimal places.

For example, walking 5 km at £2.50 per km raises £12.50.
hints: Read the distance first, then the rate per kilometre, in that order.
Cast each input to the right type, multiply them together, then round the result before printing.

tasks.title: Cinema booking
tasks.brief:
A cinema charges £7.50 per adult ticket and £4.25 per child ticket — these prices are fixed, so your program doesn't need to read them in.

Read the number of adults. Read the number of children. Output the total cost of the booking, rounded to 2 decimal places.

For example, 2 adults and 3 children costs £27.75 in total.
hints: Work out the adult subtotal and the child subtotal separately, then add them together.
Multiply each count by its fixed price to get a subtotal, add the subtotals together, then round the result.

tasks.title: Fuel efficiency
tasks.brief:
A driver wants to know how economical a journey was.

Read the distance travelled in miles, a decimal. Read the litres of fuel used, a decimal. Report the miles travelled per litre, correct to 2 decimal places.

For example, travelling 100 miles using 8 litres gives 12.5 miles per litre.
hints: Divide distance by litres used. Round only right at the end, when you print the result.
Cast both values to floats, divide one by the other, then round only the final result.

tasks.title: Packing boxes
tasks.brief:
A warehouse packs items into boxes that hold 12 items each.

Read the number of items in stock. State how many full boxes can be packed, and how many items would be left unpacked, in the format `<boxes> full boxes, <items left> left over`.

Always write "boxes" even when the answer is 1 (don't worry about "box" vs "boxes" grammar).

For example, 51 items gives 4 full boxes, with 3 left over.
hints: Whole boxes uses //. Items left over uses %.
// gives the whole number of groups, % gives what's left over — build the final line with an f-string.

tasks.title: Sports club membership
tasks.brief:
A sports club is writing software to work out annual membership costs.

Membership costs £25 per month. Members also pay a one-off joining fee of £15.

Write a program that:
- reads the number of months a new member wishes to join for
- calculates the total amount payable, including the joining fee
- outputs the total in the format `Total: £<amount>`

Assume the total is always a whole number of pounds. For example, 12 months costs £315 in total (12 × 25 + 15).
hints: Multiply the number of months by the monthly cost, then add the fixed one-off fee.
Cast the input, work out the total with the formula from the notes, then print it in an f-string.

tasks.title: Temperature conversion utility
tasks.brief:
A weather station stores temperatures in degrees Celsius but its display board works in degrees Fahrenheit.

The conversion is: Fahrenheit = Celsius × 1.8 + 32.

Read a temperature in degrees Celsius, which may include a decimal part. Output both the original Celsius value and the converted Fahrenheit value, the Fahrenheit rounded to 1 decimal place, in the format `<celsius>C = <fahrenheit>F`.

For example, 21.5C converts to 70.7F.
hints: Store the Celsius value in its own variable so you still have it to print after working out Fahrenheit.
Apply the conversion formula given in the notes to the cast input, round the result, then print both values in an f-string.

tasks.title: Payroll slip
tasks.brief:
A small business needs a program to produce a simple pay summary.

An employee is paid an hourly rate for the hours they work. Tax of 20% is deducted from the gross pay.

Read the hours worked, a whole number. Read the hourly rate, a decimal. Output three lines, all rounded to 2 decimal places, in the format:

```
Gross: 300.0
Tax: 60.0
Net: 240.0
```

Gross pay is hours × rate. Tax is 20% of the gross pay. Net pay is gross pay minus tax.
hints: Work out gross, then tax, then net — each depends on the one before it, so store them in that order.
Gross is a multiplication, tax is a percentage of gross, net is gross minus tax — three variables, in that order.

tasks.title: Delivery charge calculator
tasks.brief:
An online shop calculates delivery charges by parcel weight.

The charge is 50p per kilogram, plus a fixed handling fee of £2.99. The shop always rounds the final charge to 2 decimal places.

Read the weight of a parcel in kilograms, a decimal value. Display the delivery charge in the format `Delivery: £<charge>`.

For example, a parcel weighing 5 kg costs £5.49 to deliver (5 × 0.50 + 2.99).
hints: 50p is 0.5 in pounds. Add the fixed handling fee before rounding, not after.
Multiply the weight by the per-kilogram rate, add the fixed fee, then round before printing in an f-string.

tasks.title: Simple loan estimate
tasks.brief:
A bank offers simple-interest loans.

Read the loan amount, a decimal. Read the annual interest rate as a whole percentage, for example 5 for 5%. Read the loan term in whole years.

Calculate the total amount to repay: loan amount plus interest, where interest = loan amount × rate ÷ 100 × years.

Calculate the monthly repayment: total ÷ (years × 12), rounded to 2 decimal places.

Print two lines, in the format:
```
Total: 1320.0
Monthly: 55.0
```

For example, a loan of 1200 at 5% over 2 years gives a total of 1320.0 and monthly payments of 55.0.
hints: Work out interest first, then total, then monthly — each step depends on the one before it.
Cast all three inputs, then build each new variable from the ones before it, following the formulas in the brief.

homeworkTasks.title: Add two prices
homeworkTasks.brief: Input two prices, which may include pence. Print their total, rounded to 2 decimal places.
hints: Cast both inputs to floats before adding.
Cast both, add them, then round(total, 2) before printing.

homeworkTasks.title: Photocopying cost
homeworkTasks.brief: A shop charges 5p per page photocopied. Input the number of pages copied, a whole number. Print the total cost in pounds, rounded to 2 decimal places.
hints: 5p is 0.05 in pounds.
Cast the input, multiply by 0.05, then round(total, 2) before printing.

homeworkTasks.title: Hours to minutes
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a whole number of hours. Print the equivalent number of minutes.
hints: There are 60 minutes in an hour.
Cast the input, multiply by 60, then print the result.

homeworkTasks.title: Average of two numbers
homeworkTasks.brief: Input two whole numbers. Print their average, rounded to 1 decimal place.
hints: Add the two values together, then divide by 2.
Cast both inputs, work out the average, then round(average, 1) before printing.

homeworkTasks.title: Perimeter of a square
homeworkTasks.brief: Input the side length of a square, a whole number. Print its perimeter (all four sides added together).
hints: A square's perimeter is 4 times one side.
Cast the input, multiply by 4, then print the result.

homeworkTasks.title: 10% off
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a price, which may include pence. Print the price after a 10% discount, rounded to 2 decimal places.
hints: Multiplying by 0.9 leaves 90% of the original value.
Cast the input, multiply by 0.9, then round(new_price, 2) before printing.

homeworkTasks.title: Average speed
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a distance in km, then a time in hours (both may include decimals). Print the average speed in km/h (distance divided by time), rounded to 1 decimal place.
hints: Speed is distance divided by time.
Cast both inputs, divide distance by time, then round(speed, 1) before printing.

homeworkTasks.title: Weeks to days
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a whole number of weeks. Print the equivalent number of days.
hints: There are 7 days in a week.
Cast the input, multiply by 7, then print the result.

homeworkTasks.title: Pounds to pence
homeworkTasks.brief: Input an amount in pounds, which may include decimals. Print the equivalent amount in pence, as a whole number.
hints: Multiply by 100 to convert pounds to pence, then round to the nearest whole number.
Cast to a float, multiply by 100, then wrap the result in round() and int() before printing.

homeworkTasks.title: Pizza slice cost
homeworkTasks.brief: Input the number of pizza slices bought, a whole number. Input the price per slice, which may include pence. Print the total cost, rounded to 2 decimal places.
hints: Multiply the number of slices by the price of one slice.
Cast both inputs, multiply them, then round(total, 2) before printing.

homeworkTasks.title: Sharing sweets
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a total number of sweets and the number of people sharing them, both whole numbers. Print the result in the format `<each> each, <left> left over`, where <each> is how many sweets each person gets and <left> is how many are left over.
hints: // gives the whole number each person gets. % gives what's left over.
Cast both inputs, then build the output with an f-string using // and %.

homeworkTasks.title: Temperature difference
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a high temperature, then a low temperature (both may include decimals). Print the difference between them, rounded to 1 decimal place.
hints: Subtract the low temperature from the high one.
Cast both inputs, subtract, then round(difference, 1) before printing.

homeworkTasks.title: Pages per day
homeworkTasks.brief: Input the total number of pages in a book and the number of days to read it in, both whole numbers. Print the whole number of pages that must be read each day, rounding down.
hints: // always rounds down to a whole number.
Cast both inputs, then use // to divide and print the result.

homeworkTasks.title: Journey time remaining
homeworkTasks.brief: Input the total journey time in minutes and the time already elapsed, both whole numbers. Print how many minutes remain.
hints: Subtract elapsed time from the total.
Cast both inputs, subtract, then print the result.

homeworkTasks.title: Scaling a recipe
homeworkTasks.brief: A recipe uses a certain weight of flour, in grams, for 4 servings. Input the flour weight (may include decimals). Input the number of servings actually wanted, a whole number. Print the scaled flour weight needed, rounded to 1 decimal place.
hints: Scale by servings wanted divided by the original 4 servings.
Cast both inputs, multiply the weight by (servings / 4), then round(result, 1) before printing.

homeworkTasks.title: Battery remaining
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a starting battery percentage and the percentage used since then, both whole numbers. Print the battery percentage remaining.
hints: Subtract the used percentage from the starting one.
Cast both inputs, subtract, then print the result.

homeworkTasks.title: Volume of a box
homeworkTasks.brief: Input the length, width and height of a box, one at a time (all may include decimals). Print its volume (length times width times height), rounded to 2 decimal places.
hints: Multiply all three dimensions together.
Cast all three inputs, multiply them together, then round(volume, 2) before printing.

homeworkTasks.title: Age gap
homeworkTasks.brief: Input the age of an older person, then the age of a younger person, both whole numbers. Print the difference between their ages.
hints: Subtract the younger age from the older one.
Cast both inputs, subtract, then print the result.

homeworkTasks.title: Adding VAT
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a price before tax, which may include pence. VAT is charged at 20%. Print the price including VAT, rounded to 2 decimal places.
hints: Multiplying by 1.2 adds 20% on top of the original value.
Cast the input, multiply by 1.2, then round(new_price, 2) before printing.

homeworkTasks.title: Score as a percentage
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a score and the total marks available, both whole numbers. Print the score as a percentage, rounded to the nearest whole number, in the format `<percentage>%`.
hints: Divide the score by the total, then multiply by 100.
Cast both inputs, work out the percentage, then round it before building the output with an f-string.

homeworkTasks.title: Miles to kilometres
homeworkTasks.brief: Input a distance in miles, which may include decimals. 1 mile is approximately 1.6 km. Print the equivalent distance in kilometres, rounded to 1 decimal place.
hints: Multiply the distance in miles by 1.6.
Cast the input, multiply by 1.6, then round(result, 1) before printing.

homeworkTasks.title: Weekly exercise minutes
homeworkTasks.brief: Input the number of minutes exercised per day, a whole number, assuming the same amount every day. Print the total minutes exercised over a 7-day week.
hints: Multiply the daily amount by 7.
Cast the input, multiply by 7, then print the result.

homeworkTasks.title: Weekly pay
homeworkTasks.brief: Input the number of hours worked in a week, a whole number. Input the hourly rate of pay, which may include pence. Print the total pay for the week, rounded to 2 decimal places.
hints: Multiply the hours worked by the hourly rate.
Cast both inputs, multiply them, then round(pay, 2) before printing.

homeworkTasks.title: Theme park tickets
homeworkTasks.brief: A theme park charges £12 per adult and £6 per child. Input the number of adults and the number of children, both whole numbers. Print the total cost.
hints: Work out the adult subtotal and the child subtotal separately, then add them together.
Cast both inputs, multiply each by its fixed price, add the subtotals, then print the result.

homeworkTasks.title: Order total with delivery
homeworkTasks.brief: Input the number of items ordered, a whole number. Input the price per item, which may include pence. Input a flat delivery fee, which may include pence. Print the total cost (items × price, plus the delivery fee), rounded to 2 decimal places.
hints: Work out the items' cost first, then add the delivery fee on top.
Cast all three inputs, multiply the first two, add the third, then round(total, 2) before printing.
